paper_title: Axion dark matter: strings and their cores
notes: This paper is a theoretical/numerical study of axion cosmic string networks and axion production in the early Universe. It does NOT present new experimental exclusion limits or sensitivity projections. Instead, it performs lattice field-theory simulations to understand how the axion decay constant f_a relates to the axion dark matter density through cosmological dynamics. The paper derives a prediction f_a ≈ 3.3 × 10^11 GeV (corresponding to m_a ≈ 18 μeV) based on simulations with K ≈ 8, but this is a theoretical prediction from cosmological axion production, not an experimental exclusion limit. The paper discusses challenges in simulating the full physical parameter space (particularly the logarithmic dependence on the string core-to-separation ratio κ ≡ ln(m_s t)) and shows that axion production efficiency K is relatively insensitive to string network density over the simulated range. No experimental data, observational bounds, or detector results are presented. The work is foundational for understanding axion cosmology but does not constrain axion parameters through new measurements.
